title: Bare Array/Collection Leakage (The Naked Representation)
pattern: Exposing a raw in-memory collection (such as `Vec<T>` or `HashMap<K, V>`) as a public field on a domain struct.
why_bad: It leaks representation details. Any client can bypass business rules (e.g., adding duplicate members or a blank member name) because the collection's structure is unencapsulated.
detection: Public fields typed as raw container structures (`Vec`, `HashMap`, `HashSet`, `BTreeMap`) on domain aggregate roots.
counterexample: Plain data structures (DTOs) with no domain rules or invariants. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
source: *Practical Object-Oriented Design* by Sandi Metz (Listing 2.12, "Obscuring References"); *A Philosophy of Software Design* (p. 107).
